why: The doc sentence is verbatim (w14.md:107, first of a three-sentence lede) and the cited line exists verbatim (claude.ts:2364) -- but the claim quoted the PREMISE of a doc-comment whose later paragraph reverses it, the exact 'second half of the line reverses the conclusion' trap. claude.ts:2379-2385 continues: '**The PATH half IS built** (`appendPluginBinPath`, wired at `claude-agent.ts` and `pi-agent.ts`), so on both shipping backends a `bin/` executable of an ENABLED plugin does resolve as a bare command. This function therefore no longer records the surface as deferred'. Both halves of the claimed state are false at HEAD (working tree clean for all four files). (1) PATH IS extended: `appendPluginBinPath` (data-paths.ts:247) appends `<bundleRoot>/bin` for every root of the turn's runnable capability view (`enabledPluginBundleRoots`, data-paths.ts:200), wired on the Claude backend at claude-agent.ts:691 and :736 (node shim stays first, plugin bins last) and on the Pi backend at pi-agent.ts:5187, composed for EVERY supervised child start because 'any Bash tool call' is the documented scope. Appended never prepended, so a plugin cannot shadow a system binary. (2) NOT deferred: `addClaudeBinSurfaceDeferral` (claude.ts:2392-2435) pushes no `deferred` row at all -- it returns early when every bin file is already reached (:2415) and again whenever the bundle declares any capability (:2422); the only remaining output is a `warning` diagnostic for the single residual case of a bundle declaring zero capabilities, hence carrying no runtime root. Consequence verified separately from the identifier by positive control: `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/plugin-bin-path.test.ts` (6 tests, all pass) asserts a bundle executable resolves as a bare command on both backends, appends rather than shadows, grants nothing while the plugin is disabled, and reaches every Pi supervised child start; `format-adapters.test.ts:2817` ('defers every file-backed Claude surface it cannot run') passes with deferred kinds `['settings','theme']` -- no `bin` row. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 and not a Nessy product difference: it is a shipped fix (tracked as C6), whose stated motive was that a `bin` deferral set compatibility.state to `partial`, and management-service-v2.ts:553 purges every durable activation grant for a partial bundle on repair.
correctedState: Nessy implements the documented behaviour on both shipping backends. `appendPluginBinPath` (packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:247) appends each enabled bundle's existing `bin/` directory to the Bash tool's PATH, keyed off the turn's runnable capability view via `enabledPluginBundleRoots` (data-paths.ts:200) so enablement -- not skill selection -- is the condition, matching 'while the plugin is enabled'. It is wired at claude-agent.ts:691/:736 (node shim first, plugin bins last) and pi-agent.ts:5187 (every supervised child start). Directories are appended, never prepended, so a plugin cannot shadow a system binary. `addClaudeBinSurfaceDeferral` (format-adapters/claude.ts:2392) records no deferral for `bin/`; it emits only a warning for the one residual case -- a bundle that declares no capability at all, so nothing carries its bundle root and its `bin/` is unreachable. The comment at claude.ts:2364 is the historical premise of that doc block, corrected ten lines below at :2379.
